Question 2 of 11 · Is there a Creator?

Did the universe have a beginning?

Short answer

Yes. Planck’s measurements put its age at about 13.8 billion years.

Source: ESA, Planck 2013 (opens in a new tab)

The evidence

Or has it always existed, with no starting point?

What does the evidence say?

ESA’s Planck mission measured the age of the universe at about 13.8 billion years.

ArticleESA: Planck reveals an almost perfect Universe (2013)↗(opens in a new tab)ArticleNASA: Universe overview↗(opens in a new tab)

In 2003 the physicists Arvind Borde, Alan Guth and Alexander Vilenkin showed that a universe which is inflating, or “just expanding sufficiently fast,” “must be incomplete in null and timelike past directions.” In plain words: its history cannot run back forever.

StudyBorde, Guth and Vilenkin, “Inflationary spacetimes are not past-complete”↗(opens in a new tab)

Objections

What people say against this, and our answer. Open one to read it.

You might say“No, it always existed”

Our answer

The universe always existed — let's examine that.

Why this doesn't hold

An eternal universe would have no age. Yet ESA’s Planck mission measured the universe’s age at about 13.8 billion years.

ArticleESA: Planck reveals an almost perfect Universe (2013)↗(opens in a new tab)

What about models in which the universe has been inflating forever? Borde, Guth and Vilenkin showed that a universe which is inflating, or just expanding fast enough, cannot run back into the past forever.

StudyBorde, Guth and Vilenkin, “Inflationary spacetimes are not past-complete”↗(opens in a new tab)
You might say“Science hasn't determined that yet”

Our answer

Science actually has a strong answer here.

What the evidence shows

ESA’s Planck mission measured the universe’s age at about 13.8 billion years, and Borde, Guth and Vilenkin showed that a universe expanding fast enough cannot run back into the past forever.
